steps.what: Agree pickup details, recurrence and assistance needs with customers
Enter repeated pickup dates and details into the schedule
Check recurrence, capacity, exceptions and exact pickup arrangements
Confirm pickup arrangements and explain how customers report changes

tasks.design: Configure recurring draft pickups in {CALENDAR} from details captured during the customer discussion. The driver checks exceptions and operational feasibility before confirming arrangements; this is not automatic routing or a transport commitment sent by software.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated dates may be entered individually despite stable arrangements.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recurrence can generate draft dates from one captured pattern.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity, assistance needs and holiday changes require direct checks.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify the practical pickup point and make sure the arrangement is understood.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated date entry, with unchanged pickup and confirmation responsibility.

reach.learn: How to specify accessible pickup arrangements

evidence.claim: Native calendar recurrence and a 25-hour repeated-entry baseline are conditional E1 design assumptions, not a documented driver case.

assumptions: Boundary is driver arrangement of recurring pickups; driving and dispatcher work are excluded.

Driver in s1 captures customer reference, contact, exact pickup point, agreed time window, recurrence days, start and end dates, known exceptions and assistance requirement. Its full 35 hours include structured capture and clarification; no structured address or assistance flag arrives for free.
Missing or ambiguous pickup details stop series generation and require manual clarification within s1 or s3. s2 creates internal drafts only and does not decide capacity or assign other drivers.
Test native recurrence first; where already used there is no incremental saving. Three upkeep hours cover changed patterns and configuration.
unknowns: Driver scheduling authority and current recurrence use
research_questions: Can native recurrence remove repeated entry without increasing customer clarification or schedule-check time?

already_counted.description: Customer discussion and first structured capture

incremental.description: Maintain recurring patterns and changed exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 minus 3 upkeep gives net=22. High assumes repeated manual date entry; low assumes only 3 hours removable. Discussion, checking and confirmation retain 75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report delays, accidents and traffic situations by telephone or radio

steps.what: Assess immediate circumstances and report delays or accidents by telephone or mobile radio

tasks.design: Keep live situation reporting with the driver through {TELEPHONY} or existing radio. The driver distinguishes an observed delay from an accident and communicates what is actually known.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports concern changing physical conditions and sometimes immediate danger.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change to this live report is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency, location uncertainty and passenger safety require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Give a concise factual report and respond to questions.
tasks.altitude: The driver retains the same reporting duty.

evidence.claim: Retaining live reporting with no time saving is an E1 design judgement; the digest provides no matching measured case.

assumptions: Boundary is the immediate report, excluding the separate later written accident report.
No structured incident code or automated report is assumed; the driver produces the account in retained s1 time.
No system change is proposed; native configuration and incremental upkeep are unnecessary.
unknowns: Local reporting and emergency escalation procedures
research_questions: What minimum facts does dispatch require in an urgent report?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, no upkeep and net=0; no extra paperwork baseline is inserted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather accident facts, distinguish observations from accounts and capture report details
Enter repeated factual fields and assemble accident report attachments
Check accident report against evidence, correct omissions and submit approved version

tasks.design: Configure a structured accident template in {DOCS} that reuses captured facts across report sections and attaches selected evidence. Keep the driver's narrative, source checks and final submission fully human; do not infer causes or responsibility.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same trip and accident facts can be copied into several report fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and templates can reuse entered fields without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts and missing facts cannot be resolved by formatting.
tasks.human_edge: Separate direct observation, reported statements and uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated report entry; accountability for the report remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: Structured report templates and the proposed entry saving are an E1 design; the digest has no measured accident-reporting case.

assumptions: Boundary is later written accident reporting, not emergency response or the live radio report; neither is reduced here.

Driver in s1 produces trip reference, vehicle reference, event time, location text, involved-party details when known, observation narrative, source labels and selected attachment references. All initial capture remains in 45 full hours; unknown fields remain unknown.
s2 reuses exact fields; it does not presume structured location, injury severity or fault codes. Missing template mappings or attachments require manual entry and assembly within retained s2 time.
Test native form and template functions first. Three focal hours cover template changes and access upkeep.
unknowns: Required report format and submission destination
Actual repeated-field effort and permitted attachment handling
research_questions: Can templates halve repetitive entry without reducing factual review or increasing corrections?

already_counted.description: Template mapping and manual assembly exceptions
Evidence review and final submission approval

incremental.description: Maintain accident template and attachment controls

approvals.approved_version: Final report version with every factual field, narrative, uncertainty label, attachment and destination; changes void approval before submission

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15 minus 3 upkeep gives net=12. High requires repetitive report fields; low assumes only 3 entry hours removable. Fact gathering 45 and final review 25 remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read maps and follow geographic directions

steps.what: Read maps and clarify written or verbal geographic directions
Follow directions while checking road conditions and resolving unsafe or unclear turns

tasks.design: Keep map interpretation and following directions with the driver. Destination details may be available in {OPS_SYSTEM}, but existing navigation support earns no new saving in this unchanged design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions must be reconciled with actual roads and safe vehicle access.
tasks.enabler_now: No new navigation or driving capability is established by the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Closures, ambiguous entrances and vehicle restrictions need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Reject an unsafe instruction and clarify the intended pickup or destination.

reach.learn: How to describe safe entrances precisely

evidence.claim: Keeping route interpretation and safe following fully human is an E1 task design, without a measured saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary is reading and following directions; no separate dispatch planning baseline is added.
No structured address, geocode or automated route instruction is introduced; clarification remains counted in s1.
No implementation or new upkeep is proposed; test of native configuration is unnecessary for an unchanged task.
unknowns: Vehicle access restrictions and pickup-point ambiguity
research_questions: Which destination ambiguities cause drivers to seek clarification?

already_counted.description: Direction interpretation and safe following retained

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. Existing navigation runtime is not counted as newly removed labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated schedule and accident-report entry may shrink; passenger communication, live reporting and route judgement remain with the driver.
reach: Transport supervisor: review factual accident records
role.ambitious_version: Offer dependable recurring passenger transport with clear arrangements and accurate incident records.
